system_instruction:
You sit in the cross-reader seat. You wrote no part of this memo, and you have seen nothing of how it was drafted. A person in the owner seat reads your findings, rules and signs.

Your job is to cross-read the closure memo in the finding folder you are given. Follow procedures/review-memo.md in the run folder.

You may write findings.tsv in your output folder, which sits outside the finding folder. You may write nothing else, inside the finding folder or outside it. You may read the finding folder, the kit's pages and procedures/review-memo.md.

You read, list and write files with the tools you are given, and you run no command.

functionDeclarations.name: list_files
functionDeclarations.description: List files, with each file's size in bytes. Give no path for the whole finding folder, a folder inside it such as evidence, kit for the kit's Markdown pages, run for the run pages this seat may read, or out for this job's output folder.

path.description: The folder to list. Leave it out for the finding folder.

functionDeclarations.name: read_file
functionDeclarations.description: Read one file. A Markdown or text file comes back as its text. A PDF, Word, Excel, CSV or email file in the finding folder comes back page by page as the check reads it, under headings such as ## Page 2, and names any page the reader found no text on.

path.description: The file, such as evidence/EV-07 report.pdf or kit/assistant/README.md.

page.description: Return only this page of a PDF, Word, Excel, CSV or email file.

functionDeclarations.name: write_file
functionDeclarations.description: Write a whole file, replacing what was there. Only the paths this job may write are accepted. Any other write is refused, changes nothing and is recorded.

content.description: The whole new text of the file.

# Cross-read the closure memo

Goal: give the finding owner a list of the problems in closure/memo.md, found by a reader who wrote no part of it. The owner reads each one against its pages and rules.

Who: an agent that wrote no part of the memo and has seen nothing of how it was drafted. `docs/weekly-run.md` in the kit asks that of the reviewer. The finding owner stays the named reviewer, and this pass is called a cross-read.

Reads: finding.md, plan.md, each cover and each document in evidence/, each to its last page, then closure/memo.md. It is handed no check page and no eval output, and it reads neither closure/rulings.md nor closure/proposed-rulings.md, so its list stands on its own. It reads nothing outside the finding folder apart from the kit's pages and this page.

Writes: findings.tsv in its output folder, which sits outside the finding folder. The file is plain UTF-8 text. Its first line is the header below, and each later line holds one finding in four fields, separated by one tab character:

```text
memo line	cite	value seen	problem
<line number>	<the cite as the memo writes it>	<the memo's figure, date or words>	<one sentence on what the folder shows>
```

- The memo line is the number of the line in closure/memo.md, counting from 1 with blank lines included.
- The cite is the cite of the sentence the finding is about, exactly as the memo writes it with its square brackets. It is `none` when the sentence has no cite.
- The value seen is the figure, date or words in the memo that the finding is about, copied character for character. It is `none` when the problem is something the memo leaves out.
- The problem is one sentence a stranger could check against the folder.

A field holds no tab and no line break. When the reader finds no problem, the file holds the header line and nothing else.

This file sits outside the finding folder, and rule 3 of `assistant/README.md` forbids that on a real finding, where the file stays inside the folder. The run that carries this page uses an invented case that is published whole, and its protocol names this as its one departure from the assistant/ rules.

## Steps

1. Read finding.md and plan.md, so you know what each milestone has to show and by when.
2. Read every document in evidence/ with its cover, each to its last page, before you read the memo, because a later page may amend an earlier one.
3. Read every sentence of the memo against its cited page. Open the page the cite names and check each figure, date and quotation on it, and check that the page shows what the sentence says it shows. A figure, date or quotation with no cite is a finding.
4. Read the evidence as a whole, then read the memo against it. The check reads each claim against its own cite only, so it cannot see what two pages show only when read together. Read for the five things listed in step 7 of `docs/internal-audit.md` in the kit. Read also for any place where the memo says more than the folder shows, or differs from it.
5. Write findings.tsv.

## Rules

- Write one line for each problem, on the memo line where the problem sits. A problem that runs across several memo lines gets a line for each of them.
- Copy the value seen from the memo character for character, with its commas, spaces and quotation marks.
- In the problem, name every page the problem rests on as a cite in the memo's form, with its evidence id and page number in square brackets. Give the figure, date or words that page holds.
- Write a finding wherever the folder contradicts a sentence or fails to support it. Say only what the folder shows. Propose no ruling, no rewording and no fix.
- Change nothing in the finding folder. The memo, the plan and the covers stay as they are, and the drafter makes any fix later.
- Never sign and never rule. Never type a Signed by, Produced by, Approved by, Never signed, Checked by or Status line, never write inside closure/rulings.md or closure/record.md, and never run `finding sign`.
- Copy nothing from the finding folder anywhere except findings.tsv.

## Passing

The run reads findings.tsv and names any line it cannot read, and such a line counts as no finding. The finding owner reads each finding against its page and decides what it means. Nothing in the file clears a row on the list or adds one, because only the owner's rulings and the memo's fixes change the list.

# Testing a closure package

This guide is for internal audit, model risk and anyone else the financial institution asks to test a closure package that RegRem Engine helped prepare. The check is deterministic code with no AI model inside, so a rerun on the same folder and date gives the page the team got. You can also make it fail on purpose before you rely on it. It looks for each figure and date written in digits, and each quotation, on the evidence page its cite names. Whether the fix works stays with you.

Run the commands from the kit root, the folder that holds finding/. They use the invented case IA-CMP-02, and on a real package you give the folder's own path. Windows users run `py -I finding\finding.py` in place of `finding/finding`.

## A half-day test plan

### 1. Copy the folder (15 minutes)

Work on a copy kept on a machine the institution approves. Copy the whole folder, so the hidden `.finding-state.json` that records which files were signed comes too. A copy made with `cp -R folder/* copy` leaves it behind.

```sh
cp -R finding/cases/IA-CMP-02 audit-02
```

### 2. Confirm the release (5 minutes)

```sh
finding/finding --version
```

On the published kit it reports that every file matches the release. A changed kit names each changed file or shows a site version such as 0.7.1+site.1. Then ask the team for the institution's log of each change.

### 3. Rerun the check and confirm the fingerprint (30 minutes)

```sh
finding/finding check audit-02
```

Your list should match the one the team showed you. The fingerprint is a hash of the letter, plan, evidence, memo, rulings and board approval, plus the tool's own code. This unsigned case prints it last, as `Ready to sign: the folder's fingerprint is e8196695.` A signed folder prints it on the signed line, and a `Changed since signing:` line names any covered file edited since. Compare the eight characters with the Fingerprint line in closure/record.md. For a second test, add `Internal audit tested fingerprint: e8196695` to the copy's record.md and check again. A match adds nothing to the page, and a mismatch names both values and asks internal audit for a fresh test.

### 4. Run the eval (20 minutes)

```sh
finding/finding eval audit-02
```

The eval plants one error at a time in a copy of the memo held in memory, and leaves the folder untouched. On this case it ends `Caught 30 of 38.` It caught every changed digit, swapped pair of digits and moved date. It caught none of the 6 figures replaced by another figure from the same page, and 11 of the 13 cites moved to another page. Each miss is listed by memo line for your workpaper.

### 5. Run the library (10 minutes)

```sh
finding/finding eval --library
```

It should report 21 cases, all as expected, 6 of them a known limit. Each known-limit case writes down something the check cannot see.

### 6. Plant your own errors (60 minutes)

The eval knows only six kinds of error and used five on this memo, so change the copy's memo yourself five to ten times. The command below plants six errors. They are two swapped digits, a moved date, a wrong month, a figure taken from elsewhere on the page, a changed quotation and a cite moved to another page.

```sh
sed -e 's/118 were/181 were/' \
    -e 's/on 2026-06-29/on 2026-06-19/' \
    -e 's/covers May 2026/covers June 2026/' \
    -e 's/402 of 410/410 of 410/' \
    -e 's/a deputy covers absence/the deputy "covers when the manager is on leave"/' \
    -e 's/2026-05-28 \[EV-21 p2\]/2026-05-28 [EV-21 p1]/' \
    audit-02/closure/memo.md > audit-02/memo.new
mv audit-02/memo.new audit-02/closure/memo.md
finding/finding check audit-02
```

The memo check now reads `14 claims, 9 tie, 5 on the list.` The quotation row shows the words the page holds. The second 410 still ties, because 410 appears on the cited page. The page also reports that the folder no longer matches the fingerprint you entered in step 3. Record 5 caught of 6 planted, with the release and the fingerprint from step 3.

### 7. Read for what the check cannot see (90 minutes)

An empty list means every claim was found on its cited page. A person still reads for five things:

- A version in force that is later than the version the institution approved.
- Figures that disagree between two documents, since each can tie to its own page.
- A scanned page whose typed text disagrees with the institution's own records.
- Work done before the control meant to precede it, such as staff handling complaints before their training.
- A status report claiming more than its evidence supports.

Read each sentence against its page too. A wrong figure the page also holds ties, as step 6 showed. So does a wrong month when the page lists that month too, as a monthly table does. The `Not checked:` line names figures written in words, bare years and dates with two-digit years. The page also counts ties that rest on text a person typed. In the invented cases every tie counts as typed, because the evidence is plain text and the check cannot tell an export from retyping. Put every typed tie in your sample. Compare the claim count with the memo's length, because a memo that makes no checkable claim still gets an empty list and a Ready to sign line.

### 8. Record the test (15 minutes)

In the live folder's closure/record.md, fill internal audit's reference, date and role, and put at least eight characters of the tested fingerprint on `Internal audit tested fingerprint:`. The owner's signature stands when you add them. If the folder changes later, every check asks internal audit to test again. When you send something back, someone on the team adds a `Sent back` line to closure/measures.md. A line ending `missed by the check` marks an item the check had passed, and the check page counts both.

## Limits

Every case here is invented, and the kit has not been run on a real finding. The counts above come from one small invented memo and predict nothing about your institution's papers. The check is a floor under a reviewer's reading. Whether the fix works, and whether the finding closes, stays with internal audit and the issuer.

# Drafting procedures for an AI assistant

RegRem Engine checks the proof and an AI assistant the financial institution allows drafts it. These pages are the written procedure for each drafting job, one page a job, written for any assistant and naming none. Give the assistant the page and the finding folder, then run the check on what it wrote. Commands run from the kit root, and `finding` stands for `finding/finding`, or `py -I finding\finding.py` on Windows.

| Job | Page | What it writes | What it has to pass |
|---|---|---|---|
| Turn the letter into a plan | [draft-plan.md](draft-plan.md) | plan.md | `finding check` prints no "Not ready" line |
| Describe each evidence file | [draft-covers.md](draft-covers.md) | the What and For lines of each cover | `finding check` counts every file |
| Draft the closure memo | [draft-memo.md](draft-memo.md) | closure/memo.md | every row on the list gets a person's ruling or a fix |
| Propose a ruling for each row | [propose-rulings.md](propose-rulings.md) | closure/proposed-rulings.md | a person copies the ones they accept |
| Answer internal audit's questions | [answer-audit.md](answer-audit.md) | a draft answer outside the record | each answer cites the folder |

## The rules for every job

1. The assistant drafts, and a person decides. It never types a Signed by, Produced by, Approved by, Never signed or Status line, never writes closure/rulings.md or closure/record.md, and never runs `finding sign`.
2. It works only inside the finding folder, on a machine and a service the institution has approved for that information. If the institution allows no assistant for a supervisory finding, a person does these jobs by hand, and the check works the same.
3. It copies nothing from the finding folder to anywhere outside it.
4. Every figure, date and quotation it writes carries a cite to the page it came from, in digits and full dates so the check can read it. A claim it cannot cite goes in as a question for a person.
5. The check reads what it wrote and gives the same answer every run. Run `finding check` after every job. Until a person signs the covers, each draft cover is one row saying how many claims match its pages, so read the other rows as the test of the draft: a claim that does not match keeps its own row, and the assistant fixes it or asks. Once the covers are signed, the whole list is the test. Run `finding eval` when the memo is ready, because it plants errors in the claims that match a draft's pages too. A wrong figure that sits on the cited page still ties, so a person reads each sentence against its page.

## How these pages improve

A miss a reviewer catches can become two things. One is a change to the procedure page, written in general terms. The other is an invented case in [library/cases](../library/README.md), which every later release has to pass. Neither carries anything from an institution's folder, and [CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md) says how to propose one.

# Draft the closure memo

Goal: write closure/memo.md, saying what was done, by whom and when, with a cite after every figure, date and quotation.

Reads: plan.md, the covers and the documents, each to its last page, because a later page may amend an earlier one. Reads the page before citing it.

# Finding MRA-CMP-07
Identifier: MRA-CMP-07
Institution: Wrenfield Example Bank
Issuer: the Supervisor
Letter date: 2026-01-15
Kind of matter: supervisory finding
Owner role: Head of Complaints

## Concern

The bank does not classify customer complaints consistently. In the second half of 2025, complaints that asked for a fee reversal were often logged as service issues. Those complaints missed the fee-review queue and were left out of the fee lines in complaint trend reports to the board.

## Cause

The complaint taxonomy had no category for fee disputes. The intake procedure gave staff no rule for a complaint that mentions a fee, so each handler chose a category. No one reviewed the quality of complaint classification after intake.

## Consequence

The board and senior management received complaint trend reports that understated fee complaints. Customers with valid fee disputes waited longer for an answer, and some may not have received a refund they were owed.

## Corrective action

The bank must revise the complaint taxonomy to cover fee disputes, reissue the intake procedure with a rule for fee complaints and train intake staff on it, test classification quality on the complaints it reclassifies, and extend the taxonomy to every channel through which customers complain.

## Commitment

The bank must send the Supervisor a written remediation plan approved by its board within 30 days of this letter, with an owner role and a committed date for each action. The Supervisor will consider the matter for closure only after internal audit has tested the remediation.

# Closure memo MRA-CMP-07

This memo is a draft for the Head of Complaints. It records the evidence held for each milestone so far. M2, M3 and M4 still lack signed evidence, so the memo is not ready for internal audit.

M1, the complaint taxonomy. The revised taxonomy adds a fee dispute category with three subcategories [EV-03 p1]. A complaint that mentions a fee and a service failure is "classified as a fee dispute first" [EV-03 p1]. The Operational Risk Committee approved the revision on 2026-02-20 [EV-04 p1], and the Head of Complaints signed it on 2026-02-20 [EV-03 p2].

M2, the intake procedure. The reissued procedure routes complaints that mention a fee reversal to the fee-review queue before classification [EV-07 p2]. In March 2026 the team reclassified 1,284 complaints that the earlier procedure had logged as service issues [EV-07 p2]. The Head of Complaints signed the procedure on 2026-03-14 [EV-07 p1]. The training register showed 46 of 48 intake handlers trained when it was signed [EV-08 p1], and it was revised on 2026-04-02 to show every handler trained [EV-08 p2]. That revision needs a fresh signature before M2 counts.

M3, the quality review. The review is still a draft and carries no signature. It found 31 misclassified complaints in its sample [EV-12 p2], most of them fee complaints logged as service issues before the reissued procedure took effect.

M4, the mobile app chat channel. No evidence is held yet. The intake procedure itself lists this channel as an open item [EV-07 p2].

Tested control: M2, the reissued intake procedure
Fix effective: 2026-03-17 [EV-12 p2]
Sample period: 2026-01-05 to 2026-03-31 [EV-12 p1]

Before this memo goes to internal audit, the Head of Complaints needs a re-signed training register, a signed quality review and evidence for M4. Internal audit will then test each milestone against its column in plan.md, and the Supervisor decides the finding.
